Hi Sean / Kim —

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about the latency and cost gains we saw with Redwood Dedicated. Before we move procurement forward we have two asks from our CFO and product lead: 1) can we defer the planned tier upgrade (from Compact to Throughput) until Q4 but still lock in today’s pricing/discount structure, and 2) is there a clean way to convert our current add-on usage into a one-time credit or bundled feature so we don’t get double-billed when we flip tiers?

Short background: we expect traffic to remain steady through Q3, then spike in Q4 with a product rollout. The procurement team wants predictability — they don’t want to sign for Throughput today if usage won’t justify it yet.

Can you outline what the upgrade deferment options look like (timing, stepdown penalties if any, and whether add-on credits are possible)? We’d like a proposal we can show procurement by next Tuesday (13 Apr).

Tom — thanks for the clear ask and the SOW. Short answer: yes, we have a few standard paths that cover deferment and add-on crediting; I’ll summarize options below and flag follow-ups. I’m looping Kim since she owns pricing for NimbleCare.

Options (high level):
1) Upgrade-hold (no immediate change) — keep Compact through Q3, commit to an automatic upgrade window in Q4. We can anchor a price hold for 90 days from signature; no stepdown penalty if upgrade occurs within the agreed window.

2) Staged upgrade with banked credits — NimbleCare stays Compact today, we provision a reserved Throughput delta that can be activated later. For the interim we convert current add-on spend into a one-time credit (applied at activation) — typically we apply 25–40% of the last 3 months add-on spend as a banked credit depending on commit length.

3) Canary upgrade + rollback guard — enable Throughput on a subset of routes (pilot) for 30 days; if usage doesn’t justify full cutover we rollback and compensate via credits. Good for teams that want to test traffic shape.

Deliverables we can put in writing for procurement: a mutual action plan (timeline + acceptance criteria), quantified credit schedule, and a simple amendment template so legal avoids a full redline. If this sounds right I’ll send a one-page MAP and pricing examples.

Next steps I propose:
- Kim to confirm the credit % and example numbers (I’ll share usage data)
- We draft the MAP and a minimal amendment for legal
- Procurement and finance to confirm timeline constraints

I can get a draft MAP and two sample price tables to you by EOD Monday (12 Apr). Does that work?

Thanks,
Sean

Sean / Ben / Lauren —

I ran rough numbers against NimbleCare’s trailing three months (based on the SOW attachment). Proposed commercial structure we should offer in the MAP: 

A) Price-hold + activation credit (recommended):
- Hold Compact pricing for up to 120 days from signature.
- When NimbleCare activates Throughput, apply a one-time credit equal to 35% of trailing 3-month add-on spend (cap at $60k) to offset early double-billing risk.
- If activation postponed beyond the hold window, pricing will ratchet to published list unless we agree otherwise in writing.

B) Committed annual with staged uplift (value play):
- NimbleCare can commit to a 12-month reservation at a blended Throughput rate (10% lower than list) and we’ll apply a ‘transition credit’ equivalent to 20% of their current monthly add-on spend for the first three months post-activation.

C) Canary pilot (low risk):
- Pilot Throughput on 20% of critical routes for 30 days. If usage trend stays below activation threshold, we roll back and apply a 15% credit of pilot add-on consumption.

Operational guardrails to include in MAP:
- Explicit activation API call (no auto-activation without PO)
- Clear measurement windows (30/90-day) and reporting cadence
- Simple amendment template for legal to avoid long redlines (I’ve attached calcs).

Recommended ask to NimbleCare: confirm preferred path (A/B/C) by EOD Tuesday so we can finalize MAP and send to procurement.

Kim
